View Test Case
Preconditions
AddPassenger completed; getAddPaxOfferId/getAddPaxResponceID available. Collection variables reset before starting (SPEC.md §6.1).
Steps
  1. AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (send ResponseId/selectedOfferId = AddPassenger's IDs) -> capture resp.offerId/resp.responseId -> Book (send ResponseId=getSeatMapResponceID, selectedOfferId=getSeatMapOfferId).
Expected Result
GetSeatMap returns HTTP 200 with a non-empty offerId/responseId; the collection variables getSeatMapOfferId and getSeatMapResponceID (note the collection's own "Responce" spelling) are populated from these; Book accepts them and returns pnr/bookingToken/gdsPNR without needing AddPassenger's IDs re-sent -- this is a behavior change from before 2026-08-10, when GetSeatMap set no variables at all and Book still read AddPassenger's IDs.
Actual Result
Confirmed. GetSeatMap returned non-empty offerId/responseId (identical to the AddPassenger values); Book accepted them and created a real ticketed PNR. The Postman collection-variable assignment itself is script-side and not observable over raw HTTP - verified the field mapping it relies on (resp.offerId/resp.responseId) instead. BUG-16 (Book 409 with a silently created booking) did NOT reproduce. Unchanged from Rounds 1-17.

GetSeatMap completed; a cellCode/cellId recorded for an AvailablePaid cell; the pnr's bookingStatus/ticketStatus (per Retrieve) confirmed not yet ticketed before this check is made.
Steps
  1. AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (record cellCode/cellId) -> Book (submit passengersSelectedSeats) -> Retrieve immediately afterward, with no ticketing action taken in between -> inspect bookingStatus/ticketStatus alongside the seat-related fields.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: the immediate post-Book Retrieve already shows passengersSelectedSeats/passengerSeats/totalSelectedSeatsAmount populated with the selected seat, while bookingStatus/ticketStatus still reads as un-ticketed/un-issued (e.g. Booked, not Ticketed). This confirms the seat is attached to the reservation at Book time and does not depend on a later payment/ticketing step existing or completing. If bookingStatus already reads as ticketed/paid immediately post-Book with no intervening action taken, record that as a finding rather than assuming the AC's ordering holds.
Actual Result
The seat is attached at Book time: Retrieve, taken right after Book with no other action, shows passengersSelectedSeats, passengerSeats and totalSelectedSeatsAmount populated. GulfAir tickets synchronously at Book (a ticket number and ticketingDate exist immediately), so there is no un-ticketed window to isolate - the same caveat as every prior round. The core assertion holds.

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a confirmed offer; a specific AvailablePaid cell identified in the response.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> record cellDetails.cellID (capital ID) for a chosen AvailablePaid cell, plus its cellCode -> Book (submit passengersSelectedSeats with cellCode and cellId=<the recorded cellID value>).
Expected Result
Book accepts the token despite the field-name casing difference between the response (cellID) and the request (cellId) and attaches the correct seat, echoed back in the response's passengersSelectedSeats/selectedOffer.passengerFareBreakdown[].passengerSeats.
Actual Result
Accepted. The request sent the response's cellID value verbatim under the lowercase-d field name cellId; Book returned 200, attached seat 12C and echoed it at three places (top-level passengersSelectedSeats, selectedOffer.passengerFareBreakdown[].passengerSeats, priceDetails.totalSelectedSeats). The casing difference is cosmetic (case-insensitive JSON binding). The seat was not silently dropped, so BUG-19 did not reproduce. Unchanged from Rounds 1-17.
TC-SEATMAP-VAL-04 - Validate a cellID obtained from one offer's GetSeatMap response is rejected when submitted in Book for a different offer.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Confirm a seat code taken from one flight offer is refused when used on a different offer
Request: Opened seat maps for two separate offers, then booked on the second offer with seat 15B but using the seat code copied from the first offer's seat 15C
Response: The booking was accepted: reference OOPQEC, ticket 722137003886, but no seat was attached and no seat charge was made
Expected: The booking should have been refused straight away, because the seat code belongs to another offer
Actual: BUG-07, 13th confirmed occurrence (not new) — the foreign seat code was not rejected; a real ticket was issued and the requested seat was silently dropped without any error
Status: FAIL
Evidence
Book 200 in 30.6s; pnr OOPQEC, ticket 722137003886; passengersSelectedSeats {} ; priceDetails totalAmount 1143 SAR = base 790 + tax 353, totalSelectedSeatsAmount 0

View Test Case
Preconditions
Two independent, completed Search->FareConfirm->AddPassenger->GetSeatMap chains (Offer A and Offer B) for the same supplier/credentialsSelector.
Steps
  1. Chain A: Search->FareConfirm->AddPassenger->GetSeatMap, record cellID_A. Chain B: Search->FareConfirm->AddPassenger->GetSeatMap, obtain getSeatMapResponceID_B/getSeatMapOfferId_B. Book using Chain B's ResponseId/selectedOfferId but passengersSelectedSeats.cellId=cellID_A.
Expected Result
Request is rejected (exact status UNKNOWN -- confirm live per §7.9), since cellID appears (per its base64-decoded contents) to embed the originating ResponseId/OfferId/passenger-ref metadata and is presumably bound to the offer it was issued for.
Actual Result
STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-07). The foreign cellId was not rejected: Book ran the full supplier round-trip, created and ticketed a real booking, and silently dropped the seat (passengersSelectedSeats {} and no seat fee) instead of returning an error. Seat 15B was neither attached nor refused.
TC-BOOK-VAL-06 - Validate Book's behavior when passengersSelectedSeats.cellCode does not match the cell that cellId actually encodes.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Confirm what happens when the seat label and the seat code point to different seats
Request: Booked on a Bahrain to Jeddah flight (4 July 2027) with seat label 15F but the seat code of seat 15A
Response: Accepted: booking OODBGN was ticketed with seat 15F (the label) attached; seat 15A was not
Expected: Unknown — the system might trust the code, refuse the request, or book the wrong seat
Actual: Resolved: the system trusts the seat label and ignores the seat code entirely, with no cross-check (same finding as BUG-06)
Status: FAIL
Evidence
Book 200; pnr OODBGN; passengersSelectedSeats.PAX1 = {15F, 60 SAR}; seat 15A (the token's seat) not attached; total 1203 = 790 + 353 + 60

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed with a populated seatMapDetails covering a mix of window/aisle/middle/exit-row seats.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for every Seat-category cell, read cellCharacteristics[].padisCode -> classify each cell as window/aisle/extra-legroom/other using the reference table -> spot-check against the cell's own column position (e.g. the outermost column of a zone should carry a window-adjacent code) and description text.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: for codes present in the now-sourced canonical reference table (NDC_Integration/Resources/SeatResources/PadisSeatCharacteristic.md), the derived classification must not contradict column position or description text. Codes outside that table are logged, not failed.
Actual Result
Every Seat cell's description carries a window/aisle/centre marker and a left/right-side marker, and 0 of 3203 seats (all maps) contradict the cell's column (A/F=WINDOW, C/D=AISLE_SEAT, B/E=CENTER_SEAT). Extra legroom (LEG_SPACE_SEAT, 11 cells) and exit row (EXIT_ROW_SEAT, 24 cells, rows 12/14/15/16) are derivable from the text too. padisCode is "Unknown" everywhere, so the attributes are only derivable from description text (logged, not failed). Unchanged from Rounds 1-17.

Preconditions

Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for one segment, collect every rowNumber (check uniqueness), every zoneId per deck (check uniqueness within that deck), and every cell's column value (check domain membership).
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: no rowNumber repeats within the segment; no zoneId repeats within the same deck; every non-null column value is one of A/B/C/D/E/F (per the observed 6-column-per-row layout, SPEC.md §2.7); null column values correspond only to Aisle-category cells (cross-ref TC-SEATMAP-VAL-06).
Actual Result
All four constraints hold: 23 row numbers, 23 unique; 1 zone in deck Main; Seat-cell columns are exactly {A,B,C,D,E,F}; the 23 null-column cells are all Aisle-category. Every row's deck/zoneId resolves to the declared layout. Same across all 20 segments (decks: Main).

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a multi-passenger, multi-segment offer with a populated passengersSeatMapAvailability block.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for every passenger, read passengersSeatMapAvailability.<paxRef> -> confirm every key is a segmentRefId that also appears in flightSegments/seatMapDetails using EXACTLY the same casing -> for a sample of cellCode values in each passenger's allow-list, confirm that cell's seatPriceDetailsByPassenger (if priced) includes that passenger when the passenger is expected to be priced there.
Expected Result
Automatable assertions: (1) every segmentRefId key under passengersSeatMapAvailability.<paxRef> matches the casing used elsewhere in the same response (flightSegments/seatMapDetails keys) -- a differently-cased key for the same logical segment (e.g. "Seg3" vs "SEG1"/"SEG2") is a confirmed defect, not an acceptable variation; (2) every cellCode listed in a passenger's allow-list corresponds to a real cell in that segment's seatMapDetails.
Actual Result
The allow-list key is the full segmentRefId and matches the seatMapDetails/flightSegments key character-for-character; all 138 allow-listed codes exist as real cells and every AvailablePaid cell is on the list (0 missing). The block is nested one level deeper than SPEC.md describes (segment -> deck "Main" -> cellCode array). No casing inconsistency for GulfAir. Across all 20 segments: 0 paid cells missing from an allow-list, 0 allow-listed codes without a cell, 0 segment-key mismatches. A multi-segment offer (round trip) was also covered.

Endpoint Name: Confirm the seat availability values are limited to the known set and that walkways carry no prices
Request: Read every seat map captured this round (18 maps, 3203 seats) and listed each distinct availability and cell-type value
Response: Only "paid" seats were ever reported as available; taken seats show as an empty "no seat" cell; one bassinet seat is free for each passenger (2 entries); walkways have no price
Expected: Only the known availability values should appear, and walkway cells should have no price; anything new is logged, not failed
Actual: No blocked or occupied seats appear on this airline. Two new values are flagged, not failed: the "no seat" cell type for taken seats and a free per-passenger bassinet seat
Status: PASS
Evidence
cellCategory: Seat 3203, Aisle 542, NoSeat 49; cellAvailability: AvailablePaid 3203; paxCellAvailability: AvailablePaid 3734, AvailableFree 2 (AvailableFree entries: 8E PAX1 total 0; 8E PAX2 total 0); Aisle cells with cellDetails: 0; Blocked/Occupied cells: 0

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a confirmed offer with a populated seatMapDetails.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> enumerate every cells[] entry across all rows for one segment -> record the distinct cellCategory and cellAvailability/paxCellAvailability values observed.
Expected Result
Every cellCategory value observed is one of {Seat, Aisle}; every cellAvailability/paxCellAvailability value observed is one of {AvailablePaid, Blocked, Occupied}. If a new value appears (e.g. an "available free" state), log it and flag rather than hard-failing (§8.3 policy for UNKNOWN enumerations) -- do not assume the three known values are exhaustive.
Actual Result
No Blocked or Occupied value appeared anywhere. Two values outside the expected sets were found and are flagged, not failed (8.3 policy): cellCategory "NoSeat" (49 cells - a taken/absent seat, cellDetails null) and paxCellAvailability "AvailableFree" (seat 8E, the bassinet seat, on the A320 GF103 flight: overall cellAvailability stays AvailablePaid while every passenger entry says AvailableFree at 0.00 SAR - 2 passenger entries). Every Aisle cell has cellDetails null, so no price (0 violations).

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a multi-passenger, multi-segment itinerary; at least two distinct AvailablePaid cells recorded.
Steps
  1. Run (a): Book with passengersSelectedSeats omitted. Run (b): Book with one paxRef/one segmentRefId as in TC-BOOK-POS-03. Run (c): Book with two paxRef keys, each containing a setSegmentsSeats map with two segmentRefId entries.
Expected Result
(a) Book succeeds with no seat attached (passengersSelectedSeats absent/empty in the response). (b) succeeds as in TC-BOOK-POS-03. (c) UNKNOWN -- confirm live whether multiple passengers/segments nest correctly as sibling keys per SPEC.md §2.9's schema description, since only the single-passenger/single-segment shape has a directly-observed example.
Actual Result
All three sub-cases pass. (c) is evidenced again: two passenger keys, each with a setSegmentsSeats map of two segment keys, are accepted and echoed correctly at every location, and the totals reconcile (base 1698 + tax 1522 + seats 320 = 3540.00 SAR; each passenger paxTotalSeatAmount on the Book response = 160/160). The multi-seat Retrieve of the same booking under-reports the per-passenger seat total - filed separately under FLOW-V2-49-SEATFIELD (BUG-18).

Expected: "Free" is real; the other value is still unknown unless seen

View Test Case
Preconditions
None beyond a completed GetSeatMap call; deliberately sample several suppliers/fare classes known to include free-seat-selection fare products (e.g. Ultimate/Premium bundle tiers per §2.4's bundle rule descriptions mentioning free seat rows).
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap across several suppliers/offers, prioritizing fare classes whose priceClasses.rulesAndPenalties mention seat-related perks (e.g. §2.4's observed "Seat: row 8 onwards" / "Seat: Row 3 onwards" bundle rules) -> scan every cell's cellAvailability/paxCellAvailability value -> assert AvailableFree cells have seatPriceDetails/seatPriceDetailsByPassenger null (matching the confirmed example), and continue sampling specifically for AvailableAfterReservation.
Expected Result
CONFIRMED live for AvailableFree as of 2026-08-24 (see saved example above) -- update SPEC.md §2.7/§8.3's enum list to add AvailableFree to the observed set. AvailableAfterReservation remains UNKNOWN; if found, add with evidence, if never observed after a reasonably broad sample, record it as an unconfirmed QC-checklist-only candidate rather than promoting it.
Actual Result
Live evidence again: AvailableFree is a real value on GulfAir too, at the per-passenger level (8E, the bassinet seat, on the GF103 map, 2 passenger entries). It differs from the saved AirArabia example in one respect: the AirArabia AvailableFree cells carry null pricing, whereas GulfAir returns explicit 0.00 SAR price objects (total = base + taxes = 0) and keeps the overall cellAvailability at AvailablePaid. AvailableAfterReservation was not observed in any of the 20 segments and stays an unconfirmed candidate.
TC-SEATMAP-BND-04 - Confirm live whether any cellCategory value beyond {Seat, Aisle} (e.g. Lavatory/Bathroom, Bulkhead, Galley, Closet, ExitRow, StairsToUpperDeck, WingBox, StorageBin, RestrictedZone, NoSeat, Other, per the full backend enum) is ever returned.PASS
Endpoint Name: Find out whether any cell types beyond seat and walkway are ever returned
Request: Recorded the cell type of every cell across 20 flights on four aircraft types
Response: Only seats, walkways and a "no seat" type (taken seats) appear; no galley, toilet or other types
Expected: Unknown — record every extra type seen
Actual: Only the "no seat" type is new. No widebody aircraft are available, so the toilet/galley naming question stays open
Status: PASS
Evidence
distinct cellCategory values across 3794 cells: Seat 3203, Aisle 542, NoSeat 49; equipment 320, 321, 32Q, 32N; decks: Main only

Preconditions
A broad sample of GetSeatMap responses across suppliers/aircraft types (widebody aircraft with galleys/bulkheads/stairs-to-upper-deck are the most likely candidates for the rarer members).
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap across several suppliers/aircraft (prioritize widebody/double-decker equipment) -> scan every cells[].cellCategory value -> record every distinct value observed, comparing against BOTH CellCategory.md's enum names and the raw example's own comment naming.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- resolve empirically. Only Seat and Aisle are confirmed as of 2026-08-24; every other member (including whichever name -- Lavatory or Bathroom -- the bathroom-equivalent category actually uses live) remains unconfirmed. Do not assume Seat/Aisle are exhaustive, and do not assume the C# enum's member names match what the API actually serializes (the Lavatory-vs-Bathroom naming discrepancy between the raw example's comment and the enum source must be resolved live, not guessed).
Actual Result
Beyond Seat and Aisle, only "NoSeat" was observed (a taken or absent seat; cellDetails null; matches CellCategory.md's NoSeat member): 49 cells, e.g. 8E, 12C on the post-booking map. No Lavatory/Bathroom/Galley/Bulkhead/ExitRow/StairsToUpperDeck category appeared, and no widebody or double-deck aircraft is available to GulfAir/KSA in this sample, so the Lavatory-vs-Bathroom naming question stays unresolved.

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a confirmed offer with at least one AvailablePaid cell.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for every AvailablePaid cell, read seatPriceDetailsByPassenger.<paxRef>.{totalPrice, basePrice, taxesPrice}.
Expected Result
totalPrice.amount == basePrice.amount + taxesPrice.amount for every priced cell/passenger pair, in the same currency; no cell reports a totalPrice inconsistent with its own basePrice+taxesPrice.
Actual Result
0 mismatches in 3736 pairs. basePrice equals totalPrice everywhere and taxesPrice is 0.00 SAR (GulfAir does not split a seat charge into base and tax); the free bassinet seat 8E is 0 = 0 + 0. All amounts are in SAR.

UNKNOWN -- confirm live. Expected (per the existing price-reconciliation formula's pattern, §2.1) is totalAmount == totalBaseAmount + totalTaxAmount + totalAncillariesAmount + totalSelectedSeatsAmount, and totalAmount(after) == totalAmount(before seat selection) + totalSelectedSeatsAmount. Preconditions
AddPassenger completed with at least one CHD passenger; GetSeatMap completed and an exit-row cell (cellCharacteristics containing an Exit-seat characteristic) identified for that passenger's segment.
Steps
  1. AddPassenger (CHD present) -> GetSeatMap (identify an exit-row cellCode/cellId via cellCharacteristics) -> Book (assign that cellCode/cellId to the CHD passenger's setSegmentsSeats entry, bypassing any client-side UI restriction).
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: response status is an error (candidate error code RESTRICTED_EXIT_ROW_SEAT_FOR_CHILD, per this suite's Seat map - Seatmap.md TC-INT-BOOK-008 reference) and no pnr is created for this attempt. Candidate code is UNKNOWN-confirm-live -- not yet observed in any Postman-collection saved example; record the exact code/status returned and update this row plus SPEC.md §2.9 once confirmed.
Actual Result
STILL REPRODUCES in its worsened form (BUG-09). GetSeatMap itself lists the exit-row cell 10A in the CHD passenger's allow-list and prices it for the CHD; Book then accepts the CHD in an exit-row seat with zero validation, creates the PNR and tickets both passengers. No child/exit-row restriction exists anywhere in the flow.

Steps
  1. AddPassenger (ADT+INF) -> GetSeatMap -> Book (passengersSelectedSeats contains only the ADT's paxRef; INF's paxRef is absent from passengersSelectedSeats entirely) -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
Automatable assertions: Book/Retrieve succeed; selectedOffer.passengerFareBreakdown for the INF paxRef has paxTotalSeatAmount.amount == 0 (or the field/array absent) and no passengerSeats entries; the ADT's paxTotalSeatAmount matches the selected cell's price; totalSelectedSeatsAmount equals only the ADT's seat price, not double-counted for the INF.
Actual Result
All assertions hold. The infant needs no placeholder entry in passengersSelectedSeats: INF paxTotalSeatAmount 0.00 SAR with empty passengerSeats, ADT 60.00 SAR, totalSelectedSeatsAmount 60.00 SAR (once). Fare lines: ADT 1053.00 + INF 111.00 = 1164.00 = totalAmount. Unchanged from Rounds 5-13.

Preconditions
AddPassenger completed; GetSeatMap completed and a wheelchair-accessible cell identified by inspecting cellCharacteristics/description text.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap (identify a wheelchair-accessible cell by description/characteristics) -> Book (assign that cell to the relevant passenger) -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- confirm live. Expect Book/Retrieve to succeed with the seat attached like any other paid/free seat; there is no evidenced SSR (special-service-request) field anywhere in the current V2 Book/AddPassenger schema (§2.5/§2.9) to carry a WCHR code alongside the seat, so if Seat map - Seatmap.md's TC-INT-BOOK-014 expectation of a linked SSR flag is correct, that would be an undocumented field this suite has not yet discovered -- treat any SSR-linkage behavior found as a new SPEC.md §2.9 finding, not something to assume exists.
Actual Result
Not executable: the vocabulary (CHARGEABLE_SEAT, LEG_SPACE_SEAT, FRONT_OF_CABIN, WINDOW, BULKHEAD_SEAT, LEFT_SIDE_OF_AIRCRAFT, SEAT_WITH_BASSINET_FACILITY, CENTER_SEAT, AISLE_SEAT, RIGHT_SIDE_OF_AIRCRAFT, NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_INFANTS, NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_MEDICAL, EXIT_ROW_SEAT, OVER_WING_SEAT_S, PREFERRED_SEAT_PREFERENTIAL_SEAT) contains no wheelchair designation. NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_INFANTS and NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_MEDICAL are restrictions, not accessibility markers. Not called.

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a multi-passenger offer with a populated seatMapDetails.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for a sample of cells, compare cellAvailability (overall) against the set of passenger refs actually present in seatPriceDetailsByPassenger for that cell -> cross-check each listed passenger's presence against passengersSeatMapAvailability.<paxRef>.<segmentRefId> (the separate top-level per-passenger cellCode allow-list, also confirmed present in the same saved example).
Expected Result
Automatable assertion (structural, not value-equality, and NOT a completeness requirement): a passenger's absence from a cell's seatPriceDetailsByPassenger is EXPECTED and valid whenever that passenger is not eligible for that cell (confirmed pattern: a CHD/INF passenger restricted from a forward/exit cell won't appear there, per this same example's passengersSeatMapAvailability showing PAX3/PAX4 with a much shorter or empty allow-list than PAX1/PAX2). Do NOT assert every passenger must appear per priced cell -- only assert internal consistency: a passenger listed in seatPriceDetailsByPassenger for a cell SHOULD also have that cell's cellCode present in their own passengersSeatMapAvailability entry (if that top-level structure is present in the response). Do not assert cellAvailability == a per-passenger equivalent for all passengers either, since SeatMap QC Execution Checklist.md §11 explicitly notes these may differ legitimately (e.g. a seat blocked for one passenger type but not another).
Actual Result
Internally consistent: 240 passenger-cell price entries (120 x 2), 0 listed for a cell absent from that passenger's allow-list, 0 allow-list codes without a priced cell. GulfAir lists every passenger on every cell, so the "absence is valid" branch could not be exercised (not required). Per-passenger and overall availability DO legitimately differ on 8E: 8E (bassinet seat) is AvailablePaid overall but AvailableFree for both passengers at 0.00 SAR. For context: the CHD passenger is offered 24 of 24 exit-row cells, the already-tracked BUG-09.
TC-SEATMAP-BIZ-04 - Exploratory -- confirm GetSeatMap reflects real-time supplier inventory rather than a cached/stale snapshot.PASS
Endpoint Name: Confirm the seat map shows live seat availability rather than a stored copy
Request: Opened the seat map (seat 12C available), then took seat 12C with a booking, then opened the same offer's seat map again and a brand-new offer's map
Response: Before: 12C available for 60 SAR. After: 12C is gone (an empty cell) on both the same offer and the new offer; 179 seats became 178
Expected: Unknown — if a seat can be taken in between, the map should change, proving it is live
Actual: Confirmed live: the change showed up immediately on both. A taken seat shows as an empty "no seat" cell rather than "occupied"
Status: PASS
Evidence
Row 12 seat C: AvailablePaid (before) -> NoSeat/null (same-offer #2 and fresh offer); seat cells 179 -> 178/178; response headers: content-encoding, content-type, correlationid, date, server, transfer-encoding, vary, x-ms-middleware-request-id (no Cache-Control/ETag)

View Test Case
Preconditions
A test environment/mechanism that can independently occupy a seat between the two GetSeatMap calls (may require a second tester/session or coordination with the team -- environment-dependent, same caveat class as TC-BOOK-NEG-09).
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap call #1 (record a specific cell's cellAvailability) -> independently occupy/select that same cell via a separate booking action -> GetSeatMap call #2 (same offer/segment) -> compare the cell's cellAvailability between the two calls.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- resolve empirically; if reliably forceable, expect the cell's cellAvailability to transition (e.g. AvailablePaid -> Occupied) between the two calls, confirming a live supplier round-trip rather than a cached response. If not reliably forceable in this environment, downgrade to logging response timing/headers (e.g. absence of a Cache-Control/ETag suggesting no caching layer) as weaker circumstantial evidence instead.
Actual Result
CONFIRMED live inventory (as in Rounds 11-13). The seat was taken by this session's own booking, and both the same-offer re-read and a fresh-offer seat map dropped it immediately. A taken seat is still not reported as cellAvailability "Occupied": the cell becomes cellCategory "NoSeat" with cellDetails null. Response headers carry a CorrelationId only - no Cache-Control or ETag.
🔁Regression3 passed1 failed
TC-SEATMAP-REG-02 - Verify seatMapDetails.<segment>.{cabinLayoutsByDeck, rows[].{rowNumber,deck,cells[].{cellCategory,column,cellDetails}}} structure matches the fuller schema captured 2026-08-10, AND flag/tolerate the flat-columns supplier variant (no zones[]/zoneId) confirmed present in a saved example.FAIL

Request: Compared the live seat map response (one adult, Bahrain to Riyadh) field by field with the project specification
Response: Every documented field is present with the right type; four extra fields and a "no seat" cell type are not in the specification
Expected: All documented fields present and correctly typed; either supported layout shape accepted
Actual: Nothing is missing or wrong. Kept as failed, as in every earlier round, because the specification is out of date (extra fields: fare-check flag, birth date, document number, per-passenger seat list)
Status: FAIL

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a confirmed offer.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> snapshot the full response -> schema-diff against SPEC.md §2.7's current field list -> explicitly branch on which cabinLayoutsByDeck shape this supplier returns (zones[].{zoneId,columns} vs. a flat columns[] array) and whether rows[] entries carry zoneId at all, rather than assuming one shape.
Expected Result
Every OTHER key listed in SPEC.md §2.7 (rows[].{rowNumber,deck,cells[].{cellCategory,column,cellDetails.{cellID,cellCode,cellAvailability,name,description,seatPriceDetails,seatPriceDetailsByPassenger,cellCharacteristics}}}) is present and correctly typed. The cabinLayoutsByDeck/zoneId shape is now confirmed to vary by supplier -- do NOT hard-fail a response for lacking zones[]/zoneId if it instead provides the flat columns[] array (AirArabia-confirmed variant); do NOT hard-fail a response for lacking the flat columns[] array if it instead provides zones[]/zoneId. Treat presence of at least one of the two shapes as passing, and log which shape each supplier uses.
Actual Result
Every documented key is present and correctly typed: cabinLayoutsByDeck.Main.zones[].{zoneId,columns,cabinClass}, rows[].{rowNumber,deck,zoneId,cells[]}, cellDetails.{cellID,cellCode,cellAvailability,name,description,seatPriceDetails,seatPriceDetailsByPassenger,cellCharacteristics}. GulfAir uses the zones[]/zoneId shape and rows[] carry zoneId. The response also carries 4 fields SPEC.md 2.7 does not list (isFareCheckRequired, passengersSeatMapAvailability, birthDate, documentNumber) and a NoSeat cellCategory - the same schema drift flagged in every prior round, so kept FAIL for continuity; nothing is missing or mistyped.

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed; at least one Blocked or Occupied cell identified in the response.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap (identify a Blocked/Occupied cell) -> Book (submit passengersSelectedSeats using that cell's cellCode/cellId).
Expected Result
Request is rejected (exact status UNKNOWN -- confirm live per §7.9); no booking is created, or if a PNR is created it must NOT reflect the unavailable seat as attached -- either outcome should be logged precisely, since both are plausible failure modes for an unenforced availability check.
Actual Result
Both outcomes the test allows, and no unavailable seat was ever attached. Run 1 (the real null cellId of an unavailable cell) is rejected by a generic null-cellId check, not by an availability check. Run 2 (unavailable code + a borrowed valid token) is NOT rejected: Book created and ticketed a booking and silently left the seat out (passengersSelectedSeats {}), with no error telling the caller the seat was dropped - the same silent-drop pattern as BUG-07. Blocked/Occupied cells do not exist for this supplier, so NoSeat is the closest unavailable state.
TC-BOOK-NEG-06 - Validate Book rejects a passengersSelectedSeats.cellId value that has been truncated or otherwise tampered with.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Confirm a tampered seat code is refused when booking
Request: Booked seat 14A on a Bahrain to Dubai flight (3 July 2027) after altering the last 10 characters of the seat code
Response: The booking was accepted: reference TELSMS, seat 14A attached at 60 SAR
Expected: The booking should be refused, because a tampered code must fail the system's own check
Actual: BUG-06, 8th confirmed occurrence (not new) — the altered code was accepted; the seat code is never checked and the seat is chosen from the seat label alone
Status: FAIL
Evidence
tampered token length 323, last 10 chars XXXXXXXXXX; Book 200; pnr TELSMS; passengersSelectedSeats.PAX1 = {14A, 60 SAR}; total 1081 = 670 + 351 + 60

View Test Case
Preconditions
AddPassenger completed with 2+ passengers; GetSeatMap completed and one AvailablePaid cellCode/cellId recorded.
Steps
  1. AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (record one cellCode/cellId) -> Book (submit passengersSelectedSeats.T1.setSegmentsSeats.<seg>=that cell AND passengersSelectedSeats.T2.setSegmentsSeats.<seg>=the same cell).
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: request rejected (candidate error code DUPLICATE_SEAT_SELECTION_IN_REQUEST, per Seat map - Seatmap.md TC-INT-BOOK-009) before any supplier round-trip; exact status UNKNOWN-confirm-live. No pnr created.
Actual Result
Rejected cleanly and fast (0.2s, so before any supplier call) with a specific, on-point validation message naming the seat and segment. The candidate code DUPLICATE_SEAT_SELECTION_IN_REQUEST is not used - the envelope is the generic 400 NDC-INT-TEC-A0001 with the message in Context. No booking was created. Unchanged from Rounds 5-13. (This is a different scenario from BUG-07, which is a cross-offer cellId.)
TC-BOOK-NEG-08 - Validate Book rejects a request where the same passenger selects two different seats on the same segment.PASS
Endpoint Name: Understand what happens if one passenger is given two seats on the same flight
Request: Booked on Bahrain to Riyadh (7 July 2027) with a hand-written request that lists seat 14C and then seat 14D for the same passenger and flight
Response: Accepted: booking OURGLZ has only seat 14D; seat 14C was silently dropped
Expected: Unknown — document the behaviour rather than expect a specific refusal
Actual: Documented: a normal request cannot even express two seats on one flight, and a repeated entry silently keeps the last one
Status: PASS
Evidence
raw body carried the segment key twice; response passengersSelectedSeats.PAX1.<segment> = {14D, 60 SAR}; seat 14C absent; total 993

View Test Case
Preconditions
AddPassenger completed; GetSeatMap completed with 2+ AvailablePaid cells recorded for the same segment.
Steps
  1. AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (record two distinct cellCode/cellId pairs for the same segmentRefId) -> Book (attempt to submit both under the same passengersSelectedSeats.<pax>.setSegmentsSeats.<segmentRefId> key, or via whatever malformed-duplicate construction the request library allows).
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- since setSegmentsSeats is keyed by segmentRefId (a JSON object, not an array), a client cannot literally submit two values under one key -- this case instead documents that constraint and verifies the last-value-wins/serialization behavior of the test client is understood, rather than asserting a specific API rejection.
Actual Result
Constraint documented and behavior observed: in valid JSON the segment key can appear only once, and when a raw body forces the duplicate the server keeps the LAST value (seat 14D) and drops the first (14C) without any error or warning. So two different seats on one segment for one passenger is impossible to express, and a client bug that repeats the key is silently resolved to the last entry.

View Test Case
Preconditions
AddPassenger and GetSeatMap completed; a mechanism to force or simulate a supplier-side seat-allocation failure is available (environment-dependent -- may require coordination with the team per Seat map - Seatmap.md TC-INT-BOOK-012, since this cannot be reliably forced from the request alone in every environment).
Steps
  1. Book (with passengersSelectedSeats populated, targeting a scenario expected to fail at the supplier's seat-allocation step) -> observe status code -> Retrieve using any pnr/bookingToken echoed in the failure response (if any) to confirm no live booking was silently created with an unpriced/unassigned seat.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion (once a forcing mechanism exists): response is an error (candidate HTTP 422/502 per Seat map - Seatmap.md TC-INT-BOOK-012); either no pnr is returned, or if one is returned, a follow-up Retrieve shows the booking exists without the failed seat attached and without a seat fee charged. Exact behavior UNKNOWN -- confirm live and record; this is an environment-dependent exploratory case, not guaranteed reproducible on demand.
Actual Result
Blocked: a supplier-side allocation failure cannot be forced from the request. The probe did not provoke one - the invalid code was accepted and silently dropped (booking ticketed without a seat, no fee), the same silent-drop pattern seen in TC-BOOK-NEG-05 and BUG-07. No rollback path was exercised. A test double or a team-coordinated failure trigger is still needed.

View Test Case
Preconditions
AddPassenger completed; standard Book preconditions.
Steps
  1. AddPassenger -> Book (submit passengersSelectedSeats.T1.setSegmentsSeats: {}) -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: Book succeeds; no seat is attached for T1; no error is thrown by the presence of an otherwise-empty nested object.
Actual Result
Succeeded exactly as expected: HTTP 200, real ticketed PNR, no seat, totalSelectedSeatsAmount 0.00 SAR, no error. Unchanged from Rounds 1-13.
TC-BOOK-NEG-12 - Validate Book rejects requests with each mandatory field individually omitted: ResponseId/fareConfirmResponseId, selectedOfferId/SelectedOfferId, supplier, credentialsSelector.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Confirm a booking request is refused when any required field is missing
Request: Sent four booking requests, each missing one required item: the response reference, the offer reference, the supplier, or the credentials selector
Response: Three were refused with clear messages; the one without the response reference was accepted and a real ticket was issued (OWMWDQ)
Expected: All four should be refused and no booking created
Actual: BUG-05, 8th confirmed occurrence (not new) — a documented required field is not enforced on the booking step
Status: FAIL
Evidence
omit ResponseId 200, pnr OWMWDQ, ticket 722137003919; omit selectedOfferId 400 A0001; omit supplier 400 1001 "Select a valid Supplier"; omit credentialsSelector 400 1001 "Select a valid CredentialsSelector"

Steps
  1. Run 1: omit ResponseId. Run 2: omit selectedOfferId. Run 3: omit supplier. Run 4: omit credentialsSelector. Each run otherwise identical to the baseline, one fresh offer per run to avoid cross-run interference.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: all four runs are rejected (exact status UNKNOWN -- confirm live per §7.9); no pnr created in any run. Record the actual status/error shape once observed so this becomes a deterministic assertion for future automation.
Actual Result
STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-05). Three runs are cleanly rejected with a 400 in under a second (omit selectedOfferId: 400 NDC-INT-TEC-A0001 "The selected offer is invalid, expired, or could not be found"; omit supplier / credentialsSelector: 400 errorCode 1001 naming the missing field) - no 500s, so BUG-13 stays resolved. Omitting ResponseId is accepted: Book returns 200 and creates a real ticketed PNR, although ResponseId is a documented required field.
TC-SEATMAP-NEG-01 - Validate GetSeatMap is rejected (or returns an explicit not-supported response) when called for an offer whose isSeatMapRequired flag was false at FareConfirm/AddPassenger time.FAIL

Expected: The request should be refused or answered "not supported"
Actual: BUG-15, 8th confirmed occurrence (not new) — the "seat map required" flag is not enforced
Status: FAIL
Evidence
FareConfirm selectedOffer.isSeatMapRequired=false on chains A and A2 (and on 29 of 29 FareConfirm calls this round); GetSeatMap 200 with 138 and 161 seat cells respectively

View Test Case
Preconditions
A completed FareConfirm/AddPassenger chain for an offer confirmed (via the live capability flag, §2.2) to have isSeatMapRequired=false.
Steps
  1. FareConfirm/AddPassenger (confirm isSeatMapRequired=false on the live offer) -> GetSeatMap (call anyway, using that offer's IDs) -> observe response.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion once observed: rejected or an explicit unsupported-operation envelope is returned (candidate shape: the same {ErrorCode:'OperationNotSupported', ErrorMessage:...} envelope already confirmed live for GetOfferBundles on a haveBundles=false offer, §2.4) rather than a 200 with an empty/malformed seatMapDetails. Exact shape UNKNOWN for this specific endpoint -- confirm live and record.
Actual Result
STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-15). FareConfirm reports isSeatMapRequired=false (and haveBundles=false) on both offers, yet GetSeatMap returns HTTP 200 with a complete seat map on both. The flag is not enforced.
TC-SEATMAP-NEG-02 - Validate GetSeatMap is rejected when the request otherwise targets a valid offer but no segment of that offer's itinerary is being queried (i.e., the offer/response pair does not correspond to any real segment).FAIL
Endpoint Name: Confirm the seat map is refused when the two references come from different offers
Request: Mixed the response reference of one offer with the offer reference of another, in both directions
Response: Both accepted; each returned the seat map of the offer named by the offer reference
Expected: Both mixed-up requests should be refused
Actual: BUG-01, 8th confirmed occurrence (not new) — the pair is not cross-checked; the response reference is ignored
Status: FAIL
Evidence
run 1 (respA+offerA2): 200, 28 rows (GF181 BAH-JED 2027-06-28); run 2 (respA2+offerA): 200, 23 rows (GF161 BAH-RUH 2027-06-27)

Preconditions
Two independent completed AddPassenger chains for two different itineraries (Offer A, Offer B).
Steps
  1. AddPassenger for Offer A and Offer B separately -> GetSeatMap using Offer A's ResponseId but Offer B's selectedOfferId (or vice versa) -> observe response.
Expected Result
Request is rejected (exact status UNKNOWN -- confirm live per §7.9); no seatMapDetails should be returned for a segment set that doesn't belong to the referenced offer.
Actual Result
STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-01). Both mismatched pairings were accepted with HTTP 200 and a full seat map; the result follows selectedOfferId and ResponseId is ignored.
TC-SEATMAP-NEG-03 - Validate GetSeatMap rejects a stale or entirely invalid ResponseId/selectedOfferId pair.PASS
Endpoint Name: Confirm the seat map is refused for a made-up or stale reference pair
Request: Sent a completely invented pair, then a genuine pair whose offer had already been booked
Response: The invented pair was refused with a clear 400 error; the used pair still returned the full seat map
Expected: Both should be refused
Actual: The invented pair is handled correctly. The used pair is not refused, which is recorded as passing on the long-standing basis that re-reading a seat map is harmless
Status: PASS
Evidence
run 1: 400 A0001 AsyncPredicateValidator "The selected offer is invalid, expired, or could not be found"; run 2: 200, 149 seat cells, pair already booked (pnr OWONHK)

View Test Case
Preconditions
None beyond valid supplier/credentialsSelector.
Steps
  1. Run 1: GetSeatMap with a fabricated ResponseId/selectedOfferId. Run 2: GetSeatMap with a genuine but stale pair from a prior, since-superseded AddPassenger call in the same session.
Expected Result
Both runs rejected (exact status UNKNOWN -- confirm live); no seatMapDetails returned for either.
Actual Result
Run 1 (a genuinely fabricated pair) is cleanly rejected with a structured 400. Run 2 is NOT rejected: a real pair keeps working after its offer has been booked - IDs are not invalidated by use. Recorded PASS on the established basis of Rounds 1-13 (the fabricated-pair rejection is the defect check; reading a seat map for an already-booked offer is idempotent and is not tracked as a defect), but note the literal expected result for run 2 is not met.
TC-SEATMAP-NEG-04 - Validate GetSeatMap rejects requests with each mandatory field individually omitted: supplier, credentialsSelector, ResponseId, selectedOfferId.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Confirm the seat map request is refused when any required field is missing
Request: Sent four seat-map requests, each missing one required field
Response: Three were refused with clear messages; the one without the response reference returned the full seat map
Expected: All four should be refused
Actual: BUG-02, 8th confirmed occurrence (not new) — a documented required field is not enforced
Status: FAIL
Evidence
omit supplier 400 "Select a valid Supplier"; omit credentialsSelector 400 "Select a valid CredentialsSelector"; omit selectedOfferId 400 "The SelectedOfferId field is required."; omit ResponseId 200 with 23 rows

View Test Case
Preconditions
Three independent Hold calls (or one Hold reused up to the branch point, if the API tolerates repeated FareConfirmAfterHold calls) for the same supplier/credentialsSelector.
Steps
  1. Chain A: Hold -> SeatAfterHold -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> BookAfterHold -> Retrieve. Chain B: Hold -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> SeatAfterHold -> BookAfterHold -> Retrieve. Chain C: Hold -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> BookAfterHold -> SeatAfterHold -> Retrieve. Compare which chain(s) succeed at the SeatAfterHold step and whether the final Retrieve reflects a selected seat in any of them.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- resolve empirically. Record which candidate position(s) SeatAfterHold accepts without erroring, and whether the resulting Retrieve response shows passengersSelectedSeats/passengerSeats/totalSelectedSeats populated (§2.11) for that chain. If more than one position succeeds without erroring, that itself is a finding worth reporting (an under-constrained endpoint), not assumed to be intentional flexibility.
Actual Result
Not resolvable for GulfAir. SeatAfterHold rejects at every position with the identical supplier-level 409, so the outcome is not position-dependent (BUG-03), and no chain ends with a seat. FareConfirmAfterHold is also rejected for GulfAir (409 OperationNotSupported), so positions B and C could not even be reached the way the chain intends. Ground truth for the flow position stays UNKNOWN.

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetOfferBundles completed (bundle code + JourneyKey recorded); GetSeatMap completed (cellCode/cellId recorded for a segment within the same journey as the chosen bundle).
Steps
  1. GetOfferBundles (record JourneyKey/bundle code) -> AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (record cellCode/cellId for a segment belonging to that JourneyKey) -> Book (submit both selectedBundles and passengersSelectedSeats together, matching journey) -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: Book succeeds; response reflects both the bundle and the seat without either overriding the other's pricing (selectedOffer.priceDetails carries both a bundle-inclusive component and totalSelectedSeatsAmount, not double-counted or dropped).
Actual Result
Not executable for GulfAir - no bundle capability on any sampled offer, so no JourneyKey/bundle code exists to cross-check against a seat's segmentRefId. Not called. Unchanged from Rounds 1-13.

View Test Case
Preconditions
Each candidate supplier confirmed SeatMap-capable live (isSeatMapRequired observed true on at least one real offer) before including it in this run.
Steps
  1. For each of the 3+ chosen suppliers: Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap -> snapshot the full response schema (key names/types/nesting, not values).
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: every supplier's GetSeatMap response conforms to the identical schema documented in SPEC.md §2.7 (same top-level keys, same seatMapDetails/cellDetails nesting) regardless of the supplier's native protocol -- differences are limited to data values (cellCode ranges, characteristics, pricing), never to the shape itself. A supplier whose response requires a materially different assertion path is a normalization defect in the supplier-adapter layer (§1.3), not an acceptable per-supplier variation.
Actual Result
Not executed - a cross-supplier comparison cannot be built from one supplier. GulfAir's own response shape was checked on 20 segments and is stable (see VAL-10, VAL-11, REG-02). Unchanged from Rounds 1-13.
TC-SEATMAP-INT-03 - Capability-matrix sweep -- run GetSeatMap against every supplier confirmed or plausibly SeatMap-capable per SPEC.md §4.6, and record pass/fail per supplier.BLOCKED
Endpoint Name: Run the seat map against every supplier believed to support it and record pass or fail for each
Request: Would need every supplier on the capability list; only this airline is in scope
Response: This airline's seat maps worked on all 20 flights sampled; no other supplier called
Expected: A pass/fail table across all suppliers
Actual: Not run as a sweep. This airline is re-confirmed as supported
Status: BLOCKED
Evidence
GulfAir/KSA: 20 of 20 sampled segments returned a populated seatMapDetails; Search returned an empty offers list for BAH departures 2027-07-09 and later
View Test Case
Preconditions
Supplier roster and capability status pulled from SPEC.md §4.5/§4.6 for each run.
Steps
  1. For each supplier in scope: run the §4.7 capability-confirmation procedure -> if SeatMap-capable (or Unknown/Conditional, per §4.4-style caution), run GetSeatMap -> record HTTP status and whether seatMapDetails is populated.
Expected Result
Every confirmed-capable supplier's GetSeatMap call succeeds with a populated seatMapDetails; every explicitly-not-capable supplier is expected to fail gracefully (cross-ref TC-SEATMAP-NEG-01's pattern) rather than silently succeed with an empty response. Build/maintain the resulting per-supplier pass/fail table as a living artifact alongside SPEC.md §4.6.
Actual Result
Not executed as a sweep. GulfAir/KSA is confirmed SeatMap-supported (with the caveat that seat maps are empty for departures after about early August 2027, and Search returned no offers for BAH departures from 9 July 2027 on this run). No other supplier was called.

View Test Case
Preconditions
A valid Held pnr/gdsPNR/bookingToken available; a second supplier/credentialsSelector pair available for the cross-tenant variant.
Steps
  1. Run (1) with a corrupted x-api-key. Run (2) with a corrupted Client-Id. Run (3) with valid headers but supplier/credentialsSelector switched relative to the PNR's originating Hold call.
Expected Result
All three rejected -- exact status/error shape UNKNOWN, confirm live and reuse whatever envelope the same three checks produce on other endpoints (§7.14) for consistency.
Actual Result
All rejected. The two auth-header checks return the same 401 AuthenticationError envelope every other endpoint returns. The cross-tenant variants are rejected too, but by the endpoint's supplier-level 409 rather than by a tenant check, so they do not prove the credentialsSelector boundary is enforced here (compare BUG-17 on GetSeatMap). Unchanged from Rounds 1-13 for checks (1) and (2).
TC-SEATMAP-SEC-01 - Apply the three universal caller-facing security checks (invalid x-api-key, invalid Client-Id, cross-tenant supplier/credentialsSelector) to GetSeatMap.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Confirm the seat-map request is refused for a wrong key, a wrong client name, or another tenant's credentials
Request: Sent the seat-map request with a wrong access key, a wrong client name, a different airline system, and the same airline with another country's credentials (UAE instead of KSA) — plus extra checks
Response: Wrong key: refused. Wrong client name: refused. Different airline system: refused. Same airline with UAE credentials: accepted — the full seat map came back
Expected: All three kinds of request should be refused
Actual: BUG-17, 5th confirmed occurrence (not new) — switching only the credentials country is not checked, so an offer created for KSA can be read through UAE credentials
Status: FAIL
Evidence
control 200; bad key 401 AuthenticationError; bad Client-Id 401; supplier switch 400 NDC-INT-TEC-A0001 "Failed to deserialize the selected offer"; GulfAir/UAE with a KSA offer 200 (full seat map, 138 seat cells, same responseId); empty key 401; missing key 401; missing Client-Id 401; ZZZ 400; omitted 400
Control - valid headers, GulfAir/KSA (baseline)

View Test Case
Preconditions
A valid AddPassenger-derived ResponseId/selectedOfferId pair; a second supplier/credentialsSelector pair available for the cross-tenant variant.
Steps
  1. Run (1) with a corrupted x-api-key. Run (2) with a corrupted Client-Id. Run (3) with valid headers but a different supplier/credentialsSelector than the one used to establish this ResponseId/selectedOfferId.
Expected Result
All three rejected (exact status/error shape UNKNOWN, confirm live and reuse whatever envelope the same three checks produce on other endpoints, §7.14, for consistency).
Actual Result
Two of the three checks pass cleanly; the third half-passes. A wrong supplier is rejected (400), but switching only credentialsSelector to another valid one for the same supplier (GulfAir/UAE) is NOT rejected: GetSeatMap returns the complete seat map for an offer created under KSA. credentialsSelector is still not enforced as an authorization boundary on GetSeatMap (BUG-17, 5th confirmed occurrence).

Request: No API call — a documentation check of the project specification and requirements
Response: Not applicable
Expected: Note that these two requirements need a backend configuration audit and a log review, not API tests
Actual: Documented; the specification still says the same. These two acceptance criteria must not be marked as covered by API tests
Status: PASS
Evidence
No API call made, per the test case's own definition; SPEC.md headings 1.5 present and 1.8 present; PRD Gap #1 line present
View Test Case
Preconditions
N/A.
Steps
  1. Review SPEC.md §1.5/§1.8 (static, hardcoded x-api-key/Client-Id sent by THIS layer to the caller; supplier-side credentials are a separate, server-side-only concern not exposed in any request/response this suite can observe) and the PRD's §7 Non-Functional Requirements (file-only ApiResponse/SLF4J logger, correlation-ID tracing) for what actually governs supplier-auth and logging.
Expected Result
This case does not assert a pass/fail against the live API. It documents that: (a) User Story AC8's "securely authenticates with airline supplier APIs" describes THIS system's outbound credential handling toward suppliers -- a server-side/config concern, confirmable only via a backend credential-storage/config audit or the automation framework's own code review (PRD §7's Gap #1 already flags this as hardcoded tech debt), not via any request this Postman-collection-driven suite can send; (b) AC9's "provides logging" is confirmable only via log/observability review (PRD §7's ApiResponse logger, correlation-ID tracing), not via API response inspection. TC-SEATMAP-NEG-05 covers AC9's "handles errors gracefully" half, which IS API-observable.
Actual Result
Documented as specified; SPEC.md 1.5 and 1.8 and NDC_PRD.md Gap #1 (hardcoded x-api-key/Client-Id) re-checked and still say the same. AC8/AC9 must not be marked covered by API tests without the paired backend/config/log audit. Unchanged from Rounds 1-17.

View Test Case
Preconditions
Same preconditions as the existing FLOW-V2-49 (capability confirmation per §4.7, variable reset per §6.1). Additionally: a specific AvailablePaid cellCode/cellID identified from the flow's own GetSeatMap step, to be submitted on Book.
Steps
  1. Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (record cellCode/cellID; capture getSeatMapOfferId/getSeatMapResponceID) -> FareCheck (if isFareCheckRequired) -> Book (send ResponseId=getSeatMapResponceID, selectedOfferId=getSeatMapOfferId, passengersSelectedSeats populated with the recorded cellCode/cellID) -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
Per-family state check (§6.3 Family A) plus the new seat-specific checks: Book/Retrieve both echo passengersSelectedSeats matching the selection; selectedOffer.priceDetails.totalSelectedSeatsAmount is non-zero and (per TC-BOOK-BIZ-04) reconciles into totalAmount.
Actual Result
Book and Retrieve both echo the two seats (14C, 14D) and priceDetails.totalSelectedSeatsAmount = 120.00 reconciles into totalAmount 1730.00 (849 + 761 + 0 + 120) on both. But the Retrieve response is internally inconsistent for a multi-seat booking: the passenger line shows paxTotalSeatAmount 60.00 while its passengerSeats hold two 60.00 seats (120.00), and paxTotalAmount 1670.00 does not equal the Book response's 1730.00 or the offer total, so the per-passenger totals no longer sum to totalAmount. It reproduced on a second Retrieve and on the two-passenger round trip (paxTotalSeatAmount 120/120 for seats worth 160/160, per-passenger totals summing to 3460 against 3540). BUG-18 reproduces (2nd confirmed occurrence).
FLOW-V2-50-SEATFIELD - Verify that GetSeatMap's chosen seat cannot be attached via Hold directly, and must instead go through the new SeatAfterHold endpoint.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Confirm a seat chosen on the seat map cannot be attached through the Hold step directly
Request: Chose seat 14C on a Bahrain to Riyadh flight and then placed a hold with the seat included in the hold request
Response: The hold was accepted with the seat attached and priced (60 SAR); reading the held booking back shows the seat; the re-price step is refused
Expected: Unknown — the hold might ignore or refuse the seat field, or accept it
Actual: BUG-08, 8th confirmed occurrence (not new) — the hold accepts and prices the seat although the documentation says it has no seat field
Status: FAIL
Evidence
Hold echoed passengersSelectedSeats.PAX1 = {14C, 60 SAR}; Retrieve OnHold with the same seat; PnrReprice 409 ErrorCode OperationNotSupported "GulfAir does not exists"; holdExpirationDate null (BUG-04)

View Test Case
Preconditions
Same preconditions as the existing FLOW-V2-50, plus a recorded cellCode/cellID from this flow's own GetSeatMap step.
Steps
  1. Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (record cellCode/cellID) -> FareCheck (if required) -> Hold (attempt to also submit passengersSelectedSeats on this Hold call, mirroring Book's shape) -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- confirm live whether Hold silently ignores an unrecognized passengersSelectedSeats field, rejects the request outright for an unexpected field, or (surprisingly) accepts it. SPEC.md §2.10/§1.10-item6 currently documents this field as absent from Hold's contract based on the saved example alone, not a live-confirmed rejection -- this case supplies that live confirmation. Regardless of outcome, the flow's Retrieve step should be checked for whether passengersSelectedSeats/passengerSeats appear at all without a SeatAfterHold call having been made.
Actual Result
STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-08). Hold does not ignore or reject the field: it accepts it, prices the seat into the held offer (totalSelectedSeatsAmount 60.00) and Retrieve shows the seat on the OnHold booking, all without any SeatAfterHold call. This contradicts SPEC.md 1.10 item 6 / 2.10, which describe Hold as having no seat field. FareConfirmAfterHold (PnrReprice) is rejected for GulfAir with 409 OperationNotSupported, so the flow cannot reach its documented fourth step.
FLOW-V2-CANDIDATE-SM-HOLD-01 - Verify Search-to-Retrieve completes with a selected seat when SeatAfterHold is called immediately after Hold, before FareConfirmAfterHold.FAIL

Expected: Unknown by design — the seat should be added and shown at the end if this position is right
Actual: BUG-03, 8th confirmed occurrence (not new) — the chain breaks at the seat-after-hold step because this airline is refused outright

Preconditions

Steps
  1. Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> Hold (capture pnr, gdsPNR, bookingToken, holdExpirationDate) -> SeatAfterHold (submit supplier, credentialsSelector, pnr, gdsPNR, bookingToken, surName -- per §2.7a's documented-but-unconfirmed body) -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> BookAfterHold -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN by design. If this chain position is correct, expect SeatAfterHold to succeed and the final Retrieve to show passengersSelectedSeats/passengerSeats/totalSelectedSeats populated (§2.11), with FareConfirmAfterHold's re-priced total reflecting the added seat cost. If this is the wrong chain position, expect SeatAfterHold or a later step to reject.

It was continued to the end for information: FareConfirmAfterHold is also unsupported for GulfAir (409), BookAfterHold finalizes the booking and the final Retrieve carries no seat.

UNKNOWN by design -- same expected-outcome logic as FLOW-V2-CANDIDATE-SM-HOLD-01, but testing whether re-pricing (FareConfirmAfterHold) must happen before or after the seat is attached.

View Test Case
Preconditions
Same as FLOW-V2-CANDIDATE-SM-HOLD-01.
Steps
  1. Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> Hold -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> BookAfterHold -> SeatAfterHold (submit the now-finalized pnr/gdsPNR/bookingToken/surName) -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN by design. If seat selection is meant to be a pre-ticketing step only, expect this to be rejected (booking already finalized); if the API allows post-finalization seat changes, expect it to succeed and Retrieve to reflect the seat.
Actual Result
Blocked. SeatAfterHold is rejected with the same supplier-level 409 after the booking is finalized, exactly as at every other position, so it says nothing about whether post-finalization seat changes are allowed.
FLOW-V2-CANDIDATE-SM-HOLD-01-NEG - Validate SeatAfterHold rejects a pnr/gdsPNR/bookingToken triple carried over from a different, unrelated Hold call earlier in the same test session.BLOCKED

Expected: The stale request should be refused
Actual: Cannot be judged: the airline-level refusal happens first, so a stale identity cannot be told apart from a valid one

View Test Case
Preconditions
Same preconditions as FLOW-V2-CANDIDATE-SM-HOLD-01, plus a second, unrelated, already-completed Hold call from earlier in the session.
Steps
  1. Run FLOW-V2-CANDIDATE-SM-HOLD-01's chain up to Hold, then call SeatAfterHold using the pnr/gdsPNR/bookingToken from the earlier unrelated Hold call instead of this chain's own values. Do not proceed past the point where rejection is expected.
Expected Result
Request is rejected (exact status UNKNOWN -- confirm live), same class as TC-SEATAFTERHOLD-NEG-01 but exercised inside a full flow context rather than in isolation.
Actual Result
Actually attempted; the supplier-level rejection (BUG-03) fires before any identity check, so a stale identity cannot be told apart from a valid one. Not meaningfully testable for GulfAir. Unchanged from Rounds 1-13.
Findings12Defects7Unknown-resolution
Defect — BUG-18, 2nd confirmed occurrence (not new)
Retrieve under-reports the per-passenger seat total on a multi-seat booking: paxTotalSeatAmount counts only one seat, so paxTotalAmount and the sum of the passenger totals fall short of priceDetails.totalAmount. The Book response for the same booking is correct. (SPEC.md §2.7, §2.9, §2.11, §5.4 row 49 (SM/A), §6.3, §6.4, FLOW-V2-49-SEATFIELD)
Field: selectedOffer.passengerFareBreakdown[].paxTotalSeatAmount / paxTotalAmount (Retrieve response)
Expected value: paxTotalSeatAmount {"amount":120,"currency":"SAR"} for two 60.00 seats, paxTotalAmount 1730.00, matching the Book response
History: First observed Round 13 (2026-09-30); not exercised Rounds 15-17; reproduced again Round 18 (2026-10-10).
Impact: A caller reading a booking back through Retrieve sees a seat total (60.00 instead of 120.00) and a per-passenger fare (1670.00 instead of 1730.00) that no longer add up to the booking total, so any invoice, refund or reconciliation built from the passenger lines is short by the missing seat(s). See full bug report.
Evidence: Round-trip pnr OVMIAD (seats 14C + 14D, 60.00 each): Book paxTotalSeatAmount 120 / paxTotalAmount 1730; Retrieve (called twice) paxTotalSeatAmount 60 / paxTotalAmount 1670 while passengerSeats lists both seats and priceDetails.totalSelectedSeatsAmount is 120 / totalAmount 1730. Two-passenger round trip pnr TGDKPM (four seats): Book per-passenger seat total 160/160; Retrieve 120/120, per-passenger totals 1730 + 1730 = 3460 vs totalAmount 3540. One-seat booking THYDTQ is unaffected (60 = 60).
Defect — BUG-01, 8th confirmed occurrence (not new)
GetSeatMap accepts a ResponseId and selectedOfferId taken from two different offers and returns a full seat map; the result follows selectedOfferId and ResponseId is ignored. (SPEC.md §2.7, §7.7; User Story AC2, TC-SEATMAP-NEG-02)
Field: ResponseId / selectedOfferId
Expected value: 4xx validation error for a ResponseId/selectedOfferId pair that does not belong together
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-08-25); reproduced Rounds 1-3, 5, 6, 13 (Round 4 blocked by an outage); not exercised Rounds 7-12 and 15-17; reproduced again Round 18 (2026-10-10).
Impact: The pair is not cross-validated, so a wrong or mixed-up identifier pair silently returns another itinerary's seat map instead of failing, and ResponseId adds no protection. See full bug report.
Evidence: ResponseId of chain A (BAH-RUH 2027-06-27) with selectedOfferId of chain A2 (BAH-JED 2027-06-28): 200, 28 rows (JED map GF181); reverse pairing: 200, 23 rows (RUH map GF161).
Defect — BUG-02, 8th confirmed occurrence (not new)
GetSeatMap documents ResponseId as required, but a request that omits it still returns HTTP 200 with the full seat map; the other three mandatory fields are rejected with 400. (SPEC.md §2.7, §7.7, §8.1-item2, TC-SEATMAP-NEG-04)
Field: ResponseId
Expected value: 400 validation error naming ResponseId, like supplier, credentialsSelector and selectedOfferId
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-08-25); reproduced Rounds 1-3, 5, 6, 13 (not reproduced in Round 4); not exercised Rounds 7-12 and 15-17; reproduced again Round 18 (2026-10-10).
Impact: A required field is not enforced, so integrations that forget ResponseId work by accident and the documented contract cannot be trusted. See full bug report.
Evidence: omit supplier 400 "Select a valid Supplier"; omit credentialsSelector 400; omit selectedOfferId 400 "The SelectedOfferId field is required."; omit ResponseId 200 with 23 rows.
Defect — BUG-15, 8th confirmed occurrence (not new)
GetSeatMap returns HTTP 200 with a complete seat map for offers whose FareConfirm reports isSeatMapRequired=false; the flag is not enforced. (SPEC.md §2.2, §2.4, §2.7, §7.7; User Story AC2, TC-SEATMAP-NEG-01)
Field: isSeatMapRequired (FareConfirm) vs GetSeatMap response
Expected value: Rejection or an explicit not-supported envelope for an offer with isSeatMapRequired=false
History: Failing since Round 1 (2026-08-25), filed as its own BUG-15 in Round 5; reproduced Rounds 1-6 and 13; not exercised Rounds 7-12 and 15-17; reproduced again Round 18 (2026-10-10).
Impact: The capability flag cannot be used to decide whether to show seat selection, and callers get seat data for offers that are not flagged as seat-map offers. See full bug report.
Evidence: FareConfirm selectedOffer.isSeatMapRequired=false on all 29 calls this round; GetSeatMap 200 with 138 and 161 seat cells on chains A and A2.
Defect — BUG-17, 5th confirmed occurrence (not new)
GetSeatMap does not reject a request whose credentialsSelector differs from the one the offer was created under (same supplier, different valid selector). (SPEC.md §7.14; User Story AC8 ("securely authenticates" -- caller-facing half only, see TC-SEATMAP-SEC-02), TC-SEATMAP-SEC-01)
Field: credentialsSelector
Expected value: 4xx rejection (offer not found / not authorized for this credentialsSelector), as happens when the supplier is switched
History: First observed Round 11 (2026-09-29); reproduced Rounds 12 and 13 (2026-09-30) and Round 17 (2026-10-10); reproduced again Round 18 (2026-10-10).
Impact: credentialsSelector is the per-tenant boundary; a caller holding an offerId/responseId from one tenant (KSA) can read that offer's seat map through another tenant's selector (UAE), so cross-tenant isolation rests only on offer IDs being unguessable. Other offer-consuming endpoints were not tested. See full bug report.
Evidence: Offer created under GulfAir/KSA; GetSeatMap with GulfAir/UAE -> 200, full seat map, same responseId; supplier switched to TravelportNdc/UAE -> 400 NDC-INT-TEC-A0001; invalid key / Client-Id -> 401.
Defect — BUG-07, 13th confirmed occurrence (not new)
Book accepts a cellId that was issued for a different offer's seat map: it runs the full booking, tickets it, and silently drops the seat (empty passengersSelectedSeats, no fee) instead of returning an error. (SPEC.md §2.7, §2.9, §7.7, TC-SEATMAP-VAL-04)
Field: passengersSelectedSeats.<paxRef>.setSegmentsSeats.<segmentRefId>.cellId
Expected value: 4xx validation error rejecting a cellId that does not belong to this offer, with no booking created
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-08-25); confirmed Rounds 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 17 (Round 4 blocked by an outage); reproduced again Round 18 (2026-10-10).
Impact: The cellId token is not validated, so a stale or foreign token produces a booking with no seat and no error - the caller believes a seat was reserved. The same silent drop also happens for an unavailable or non-existent cellCode (TC-BOOK-NEG-05, TC-BOOK-NEG-09). See full bug report.
Evidence: Book on offer E2 (cellCode 15B) with the cellId of seat 15C from offer E1: 200, pnr OOPQEC, ticket 722137003886, passengersSelectedSeats {}, totalSelectedSeatsAmount 0, no error.
Defect — BUG-06, 8th confirmed occurrence (not new)
Book accepts a tampered cellId (last 10 characters replaced) and books the seat named by cellCode; the token is never validated (also true for a cellId belonging to a different seat, TC-BOOK-VAL-06). (SPEC.md §2.7, §2.9, §7.7, TC-BOOK-NEG-06)
Field: passengersSelectedSeats.<paxRef>.setSegmentsSeats.<segmentRefId>.cellId
Expected value: 4xx rejection of a token that fails the server-side decode/signature check
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-08-25); reproduced Rounds 1-6 and 13; not exercised Rounds 7-12 and 15-17; reproduced again Round 18 (2026-10-10).
Impact: The opaque cellId adds no integrity protection; the seat is chosen from the free-text cellCode alone, so forged or mismatched tokens are accepted. See full bug report.
Evidence: Book (cellCode 14A, cellId with trailing XXXXXXXXXX): 200, pnr TELSMS, seat 14A attached at 60.00 SAR; Book (cellCode 15F, cellId of 15A): 200, pnr OODBGN, seat 15F attached.
Defect — BUG-05, 8th confirmed occurrence (not new)
Book documents ResponseId as required, but a Book request that omits it is accepted and creates a real, ticketed PNR; the other three mandatory fields are rejected with 400. (SPEC.md §2.9, §7.7, §8.1-item2; SeatMap QC Execution Checklist.md §20, TC-BOOK-NEG-12)
Field: ResponseId
Expected value: 400 validation error naming ResponseId, no PNR created
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-08-25); reproduced Rounds 1-6 and 13; not exercised Rounds 7-12 and 15-17; reproduced again Round 18 (2026-10-10).
Impact: A required field is unenforced on the highest-blast-radius endpoint, and a malformed request still produces a real ticketed booking. See full bug report.
Evidence: omit ResponseId 200, pnr OWMWDQ; omit selectedOfferId 400 A0001; omit supplier 400 1001; omit credentialsSelector 400 1001.
Defect — BUG-09, 10th confirmed occurrence (not new)
A child passenger can be assigned an exit-row seat: GetSeatMap offers and prices all 24 exit-row cells to the CHD, and Book accepts the assignment, creates the PNR and tickets both passengers. (SPEC.md §2.7 (cellCharacteristics), §2.9; NDC_Integration/Resources/SeatMap QC Execution Checklist.md Part 1 §15; Seat map - Seatmap.md TC-INT-BOOK-008, TC-BOOK-BIZ-05)
Field: passengersSelectedSeats.<paxRef> (CHD) / GetSeatMap passengersSeatMapAvailability
Expected value: Exit-row cells absent from the CHD passenger's allow-list, and Book rejecting the assignment (candidate RESTRICTED_EXIT_ROW_SEAT_FOR_CHILD) with no PNR created
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-08-25); confirmed Rounds 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 9, re-confirmed Round 12; reproduced Round 13; not exercised Rounds 15-17; reproduced again Round 18 (2026-10-10).
Impact: A safety rule (no children in exit rows) is enforced nowhere in the API; the seat map even labels exit rows NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_INFANTS and NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_MEDICAL but has no child restriction, so any client that calls the API directly can ticket a child in an exit row. See full bug report.
Evidence: ADT + CHD offer (BAH-DMM 2027-07-05): PAX2 (CHD) allow-list contains 10A and all 24 exit-row cells; Book 200, pnr OPTSKU, PAX2 seat 10A 60.00 SAR, both passengers ticketed.
Defect — BUG-03, 8th confirmed occurrence (not new)
SeatAfterHold rejects every call for supplier GulfAir with HTTP 409 OperationNotSupported ("GulfAir does not exists") before reading any field, while GulfAir offers are Hold-capable and Hold succeeds. (SPEC.md §2.7a, TC-SEATAFTERHOLD-POS-01)
Field: SeatAfterHold response (supplier registration)
Expected value: 200 with the seat-selection response (or a documented validation error), or GulfAir being flagged as not supporting the operation before Hold is offered
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-08-25); reproduced Rounds 1-6 and 13; not exercised Rounds 7-12 and 15-17; reproduced again Round 18 (2026-10-10).
Impact: The Hold branch has no working seat-selection path for GulfAir, and six dependent test cases (VAL-01, NEG-01, NEG-02, VAL-02, INT-04, the candidate flows) cannot be evaluated. The same supplier-level 409 is also returned by FareConfirmAfterHold (PnrReprice). See full bug report.
Evidence: SeatAfterHold 409 OperationNotSupported on 9 of 9 calls with valid credentials (every chain position, mismatched and stale identities, extra field, cross-tenant variants); Holds TFBYUM and TFXRXD 200 in the same run.
Defect — BUG-04, 8th confirmed occurrence (not new)
Hold returns holdExpirationDate null for GulfAir on every call, so a Held booking has no known expiry. (SPEC.md §2.7a, §2.12, §6.5, TC-SEATAFTERHOLD-NEG-02)
Field: holdExpirationDate
Expected value: "2026-10-11T14:32:10Z" (a future ISO-8601 timestamp)
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-08-25); reproduced every round through Round 6 and in Round 13; not exercised Rounds 7-12 and 15-17; reproduced again Round 18 (2026-10-10).
Impact: Downstream cannot compute when a hold lapses, so expiry-based cleanup, the expired-hold negative tests and any customer-facing hold timer cannot work. See full bug report.
Evidence: holdExpirationDate null on 7 of 7 Hold calls this round (TLTTGU, OOEMOB, OSLGYN, TFBYUM, OODMJW, ORVBTX, TFXRXD).
Defect — BUG-08, 8th confirmed occurrence (not new)
Hold, documented as having no seat field, accepts passengersSelectedSeats, prices the seat into the held offer and Retrieve shows it on the OnHold booking, with no SeatAfterHold call. (SPEC.md §2.7a, §2.9, §2.10, §5.4 row 50 (SM/B), §5.5-item8, FLOW-V2-50-SEATFIELD)
Field: Hold request: passengersSelectedSeats
Expected value: The field ignored or rejected (per the documented contract), or the contract updated to say Hold honors seats
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-08-25); reproduced Rounds 1-3, 5, 6, 13 (Round 4 blocked by an outage); not exercised Rounds 7-12 and 15-17; reproduced again Round 18 (2026-10-10).
Impact: The documented asymmetry between the Book and Hold branches is wrong for GulfAir, and an unvalidated seat selection (same unvalidated cellId as BUG-06/07) can be attached to a hold. See full bug report.
Evidence: Hold ORVBTX with passengersSelectedSeats.PAX1 {14C}: 200, seat echoed at 60.00 SAR, totalSelectedSeatsAmount 60; Retrieve bookingStatus OnHold with the same seat.
Unknown-resolution
cellAvailability/paxCellAvailability value "AvailableFree" is real on GulfAir too, but at the per-passenger level: seat 8E (bassinet seat) on the A320 GF103 flight shows paxCellAvailability AvailableFree for every passenger with explicit 0.00 SAR price objects, while the overall cellAvailability stays AvailablePaid. Differs from the AirArabia example, whose AvailableFree cells have null pricing. (TC-SEATMAP-BND-03)

cellCategory "NoSeat" is a real value: a taken or absent seat is returned as cellCategory NoSeat with cellDetails null and column set (it never becomes Occupied/Blocked). No other category appeared on 20 narrowbody segments (aircraft 320, 321, 32Q, 32N). (TC-SEATMAP-BND-04)

FareConfirmAfterHold (PnrReprice) is not supported for GulfAir: 409 OperationNotSupported "GulfAir does not exists" on 4 of 4 calls, the same envelope as SeatAfterHold. BookAfterHold works without it (200, ticketed), so the documented Family B chain cannot be followed step by step for this supplier. (FLOW-V2-CANDIDATE-SM-HOLD-02)

When a raw Book body repeats the same segmentRefId key twice under setSegmentsSeats, the server keeps the last value and drops the first without any error (System.Text.Json-style last-wins). (TC-BOOK-NEG-08)
Unknown-resolution
A schema-valid but non-existent cellCode ("99Z", with a real cellId borrowed from another seat) and an unavailable cellCode (NoSeat 12C with a borrowed cellId) are both accepted by Book with HTTP 200 and silently dropped: a ticketed booking is created with no seat and no fee. Same silent-drop family as BUG-07; a null cellId is the only rejected form (400 "CellId is required."). (TC-BOOK-NEG-09)
Unknown-resolution
GulfAir seat descriptions include two restriction values: NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_INFANTS (exit-row cells only) and NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_MEDICAL (exit-row cells plus a few rear rows). There is still no wheelchair/accessibility value and no NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_CHILDREN value. (TC-BOOK-BIZ-07)
Unknown-resolution
Book rejects a duplicate seat inside one request in 0.2s (before any supplier call) with the generic envelope {ErrorCode NDC-INT-TEC-A0001, Context "Seat '17C' is assigned to multiple passengers on segment ..."}; the candidate code DUPLICATE_SEAT_SELECTION_IN_REQUEST is not used. Validation errors come in two envelope shapes: PascalCase {Status, ErrorCode "NDC-INT-TEC-A0001"} and camelCase {status, errorCode "1001"}. (TC-BOOK-NEG-07)

BUG-16 (Book returns an error while silently creating the booking) — exercised by TC-SEATMAP-POS-02, TC-SEATMAP-VAL-03, TC-SEATMAP-VAL-04, TC-BOOK-POS-03, TC-BOOK-BND-03. All 15 Book calls that reached the supplier (29s, 29s, 31s, 28s, 45s, 31s, 31s, 42s, 48s, 51s, 41s, 40s, 41s, 42s, 31s) and all 3 BookAfterHold calls returned a clean HTTP 200 with a pnr and bookingToken; none returned 409 NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999 or 500. It is intermittent across rounds (Round 12 saw it on 4 of 4 Book calls), so recommend a wider re-verification before closing.

BUG-19 (Book silently drops a valid same-offer seat selection) — exercised by TC-SEATMAP-VAL-03, TC-BOOK-POS-03, TC-BOOK-BND-03, TC-BOOK-BIZ-06, TC-BOOK-NEG-08. Every Book call that selected a real seat on its own offer (seat 12C, 14C, 14D, 14A, 15F, 10A, the round-trip seats and the Hold with 14C) attached the seat, priced it and echoed it. Only the deliberate invalid selections (foreign cellId, non-existent or unavailable cellCode) were dropped. Round 15 reproduced 2 of 2; Rounds 16-18 did not, so the defect still looks intermittent.
